---

To understand how a computer reads data from a Solid-State Drive (SSD), it is essential to first recognize that an SSD is fundamentally different from a traditional Hard Disk Drive (HDD). While an HDD uses spinning magnetic platters and a moving read/write head, an SSD relies entirely on flash memory—specifically, NAND flash memory chips. This architecture allows for near-instantaneous data access, as there are no mechanical parts to move.
